findings.reason: the section should first diagnose why _compatibility_census does not use stencil_nulls' degree kernel and route to it if it can, rather than author a parallel detector.
findings.text: §3 proposes a centroid-free saddle detector as new work, but gradient_cell_degree already returns the signed winding degree of the native gradient (a saddle has index -1) with a boundary-vector margin, and critical_point_candidates_batch is the production kernel ("confidence evidence can defer an uncertain nonzero-degree orbit, but cannot make it disappear"); both named candidates — local quadratic for a saddle-type Hessian, and a vertex-centred census — already exist as benchmarks/dual_stencil_census.py and benchmarks/vertex_ring_census.py, so the plan is rebuilding a solved problem instead of attributing why the forward operator's compatibility census does not route through the degree kernel.

findings.reason: the plan must either extend _local_fit_census or state the measured reason it cannot, else the census grows a second authority for the same stationary point.
findings.text: §3's ring-local-quadratic candidate is a second implementation of the same quadratic fit already in _local_fit_census (determinant of the scaled quadratic coefficient, determinant<0 classifying kind 0 = saddle, stationary point accepted when inside_or_near_source_cell within 0.25 source pitch); adding a parallel ring-only variant layers surface over the existing fit without stating why the existing fit cannot be the thing extended.

findings.reason: the plan already carries followup f-trcr-rescope-against-contour-tree (2026-10-01) instructing exactly this re-scope, so the finding is recorded rather than new.
findings.text: §1 (containment on the class-free read) and §3 (saddle detection) overlap the contour-tree topology authority, which already defines the topology order, the hex-cell carrier, critical_type and the 256/255-capacity contract over the same fields.

findings.reason: §4 should extend the existing drift-anchor bisect rather than build a second revision-tabulation path, or name the measured gap that makes the existing instrument insufficient.
findings.text: §4 proposes to "solve the diverted 110 and  the 300 rows through the certificate driver at four revisions in fresh-process lanes and tabulate per revision the terminal residual, step count and whether the NaN appears; name the commit that moved each row", but benchmarks/bank_drift_anchor_bisect.py and benchmarks/bank_drift_paired_probe.py already own revision-bisect drift attribution, and benchmarks/solovev_certificate_current_pin.py owns the certificate pin.

findings.reason: §2's done-when should name the existing driver/script as the instrument, so the regeneration is attributable to a known revision rather than to an unnamed new job.
findings.text: §2 proposes to "regenerate the twelve rows and the sixteen-row Solovev certificate in one H200 job", but benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py already defines CASE_NAMES/REQUESTED_CELLS (-110,-300,-500,-1000,-2500), the terminal-residual bound and the NaN census, and scripts/regenerate_solovev_certificate.sh already submits that driver to an H200 with a declared configuration and log root; the plan neither names nor extends this owner.

findings.reason: §5 should extend the registered-observable acceptance (adding the read/admission and position-bound criteria to that registry) rather than add a third verdict path, so a joint verdict cannot diverge from the per-observable ones already emitted.
findings.text: §5's "joint qualification rule" (residual, admitted read and resolution-scaled position bound holding together) duplicates the remit of evaluate_observable_bound_acceptance, which already applies every registered terminal-observable bound and returns a per-observable verdict, and of domain.saddle_qualified_domains (nova/equilibrium/domain.py:222), which already retains a private-flux region on a qualified saddle.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan proposes no new shallow module; §1's landed change deepens the existing per-pass evaluation in nova/equilibrium/topology.py rather than adding surface, and §3/§5 name mechanisms rather than new module families.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3's detector duplicates the degree kernel owned by nova/equilibrium/stencil_nulls.py, §4's revision-bisect drift attribution duplicates benchmarks/bank_drift_anchor_bisect.py, and §5's joint verdict duplicates the registered terminal-observable acceptance owned by nova/equilibrium/observable_acceptance.py.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the plan's sections add only internal machinery (a detector, a bank/certificate regeneration and a joint per-row verdict) and add nothing to any of the four tracked families, so no section has surface to retire or merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3 offers two "candidate" saddle detectors without citing nova/equilibrium/stencil_nulls.py, whose gradient_cell_degree/critical_point_candidates_batch already implement a centroid-free (winding-degree) critical-point census, and without citing the benchmark scripts that already prototype both candidates (benchmarks/vertex_ring_census.py, benchmarks/dual_stencil_census.py); §2/§4 likewise do not cite benchmarks/solovev_certificate.py or benchmarks/bank_drift_anchor_bisect.py.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3's first candidate ("test every ring's local quadratic for a saddle-type Hessian with its stationary point inside the ring") is precisely what forward_operator._local_fit_census already computes, and the plan gives no reason that quadratic route cannot be extended in place rather than re-authored.
